title: Hideo Kojima
wiki_lead:
Hideo Kojima (小島 秀夫, Kojima Hideo; born August 24, 1963) is a Japanese video game designer, writer, director, and producer. He is best known for the Metal Gear franchise, which remains his most famous and acclaimed work. His games are noted for being highly cinematic, the result of a passion for film and literature which began during his childhood, and he is regarded as a pioneering auteur of video games.
Upon joining Konami in 1986, Kojima directed, designed, and wrote Metal Gear (1987) for the MSX2. The game laid the foundation for the stealth game genre and the renowned Metal Gear franchise, which he continued to direct for 28 years up to Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain (2015). During his time at Konami, he created Boktai and produced Zone of the Enders and Castlevania: Lords of Shadow, as well as directing Snatcher (1988) and Policenauts (1994), which were graphic adventure games that came to be regarded for their cinematic presentation.
Kojima founded Kojima Productions within Konami in 2005, and in 2011 he was appointed vice president of Konami Digital Entertainment. In 2014, Kojima was revealed as the director for Silent Hills, the next installment in the Silent Hill franchise, via the playable teaser P.T. which has been cited as one of the greatest horror games of all time. However, the game was cancelled by Konami in 2015, shortly before Kojima's departure from the company. He then re-established Kojima Productions as an independent studio in December 2015, and, in partnership with Sony, released his first games outside Konami with Death Stranding (2019) and Death Stranding 2: On the Beach (2025).  
Following the end of his studio's collaboration with Sony, Kojima is directing the upcoming games OD and Physint in association with Xbox. A longtime film enthusiast, he announced in 2019 that his studio would expand into film production, and is currently serving as producer for three Death Stranding adaptations.

Early life
Kojima was born in the Setagaya ward of Tokyo on August 24, 1963. He has two older siblings. His father, Kingo, was a pharmacist who frequently traveled for business and named his son Hideo as it was the most common name among the doctors he met. He moved with his family to Osaka at the age of four; he later described this stage of his early life as an abrupt change of environment that led him to spend much of his time thereafter indoors, where he would watch television or make figurines. His parents were passionate about cinema—especially European films, horror, and Wild West—and began a nightly tradition of watching a film with their children, who were not allowed to go to bed until the film had finished; his parents also did not limit the type of films the children were allowed to see, regardless of content.

grok_lead: Hideo Kojima (å°å³¶ ç§å¤«, born August 24, 1963) is a Japanese video game designer, director, producer, writer, and studio founder recognized for pioneering stealth gameplay mechanics and cinematic storytelling in interactive media. After joining Konami in 1986 as one of its first dedicated game designers, Kojima developed the original Metal Gear in 1987 for the MSX2 platform, introducing core elements of tactical espionage action that defined the series spanning multiple sequels and platforms over nearly three decades. His tenure at Konami also encompassed titles like Snatcher and Policenauts, which experimented with adventure game formats influenced by film noir and science fiction, emphasizing narrative depth over conventional gameplay. Following a corporate restructuring at Konami in 2015, Kojima established Kojima Productions as an independent studio in Tokyo. There he directed Death Stranding (2019) and its sequel Death Stranding 2: On the Beach (2025), titles blending open-world exploration with themes of connection and isolation that garnered critical acclaim for their ambitious integration of player agency and philosophical undertones. As of 2026 the studio is developing the horror game OD (in collaboration with filmmaker Jordan Peele) and the action-espionage title Physint (a spiritual successor to Metal Gear), both published by Xbox Game Studios. Kojima's contributions have earned him prestigious honors, including the BAFTA Fellowship in 2020 for outstanding achievement in video games and Japan's Order of Culture commendation via the Minister of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology Award for Fine Arts in 2022, acknowledging his role in elevating video games as a medium for artistic expression. His designs consistently feature intricate plots critiquing militarism, technology's societal impacts, and human conflict, often drawing from real-world geopolitics and personal reflections on mortality, while innovating through long cutscenes, voice acting, and multimedia integration that blur lines between gaming and cinema.
